originalTitle: Show HN: A language model that lives in a boot sector
content: All the ideas came from the boot sector demo scene where people had been writing chess and BASIC games in 512 bytes, even a C compiler. I wondered what one can do using a neural network instead of a program and generating boot logs for non-existent hardware was something fun to try. Entire inference engine is 510 bytes of MBR, weights, vocab, and strings reside in the sectors following MBR. Small char-level neural network was trained on dmesg generated by machine, so machine produces Linux boot messages infinitely. train.py performs precisely the same integer arithmetic operations as the asm code does and thus produces an output identical character-by-character to the one produced by QEMU. The difference analysis revealed my favorite bug. The characters at the beginning matched those generated by the simulator, but then the output diverged. I retrieved the hidden layer via QEMU’s debug port and compared the neurons' values with those of the simulator, one neuron at a time. Only the value of the first neuron was correct. The activation involves idiv, and idiv stores its remainder in edx. The pointer to the biases table was stored in edx, which resulted in the first neuron being biased correctly and the following ones using garbage. Now the bias' address is determined from the loop counter, and no pointers have to survive the division. Another bug I found simply by looking at the code before I did my first run-through: the BIOS print routine zeros out bx, but bx contains the predicted character number. This explains the push and pop of bx surrounding the print. sectorllm is the most similar to my project, as it runs an actual 5-layer llama2 with attention mechanism in just 1.2K of assembly code. It is the trade-off in the opposite direction, as my engine needs to fit into one sector and therefore my network has just one hidden layer of int8 operations for dreaming the dmesg.
chineseTitle: Show HN：位于引导扇区的语言模型
chineseContent: 所有的想法都来自引导扇区演示场景，人们一直在用 512 字节编写国际象棋和 BASIC 游戏，甚至还有 C 编译器。我想知道使用神经网络而不是程序可以做什么，并且为不存在的硬件生成启动日志是一种有趣的尝试。整个推理引擎是510字节的MBR，权重、词汇和字符串驻留在MBR后面的扇区中。小型字符级神经网络在机器生成的 dmesg 上进行训练，因此机器可以无限地生成 Linux 启动消息。 train.py 执行与 asm 代码完全相同的整数算术运算，从而产生与 QEMU 产生的输出相同的逐个字符的输出。差异分析揭示了我最喜欢的错误。开始时的字符与模拟器生成的字符匹配，但随后输出出现分歧。我通过 QEMU 的调试端口检索隐藏层，并将神经元的值与模拟器的值进行比较，一次一个神经元。只有第一个神经元的值是正确的。激活涉及到 idiv，idiv 将其余数存储在 edx 中。指向偏差表的指针存储在 edx 中，这导致第一个神经元被正确偏置，而后续神经元则使用垃圾。现在，偏置的地址是由循环计数器确定的，并且没有指针必须在除法之后幸存下来。在第一次运行之前，我通过查看代码发现了另一个错误：BIOS 打印例程将 bx 清零，但 bx 包含预测的字符数。这解释了打印周围的 bx 的推送和弹出。 ectorllm 与我的项目最相似，因为它仅用 1.2K 的汇编代码运行一个带有注意力机制的实际 5 层 llama2。这是相反方向的权衡，因为我的引擎需要适应
